text:
They have come.

They invade the blood.

They smell of feathers,

of lack,

of weeping.

But you feed fear

and solitude

like two small animals

lost in the desert.


They have come

to set fire to the age of dream.

A farewell is your life.

But you embrace yourself

like the mad snake of motion

that finds only itself

because there is no one.


You weep beneath the weeping,

you open the chest of your desires

and you are richer than night.


But there is so much solitude

that words kill themselves.

translation.title: They Have Come...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated arrival and the stark final image of words killing themselves.
